label: FIXTURE RESULT: Stage 3 pilot (live recorded window), not the evaluation

report.summary: Outbox publications to the consumer lagged arrivals for ~100 s. The backlog built up and then drained. The slow consumer handler (~405 ms on some deliveries) is the likely cause. Transfers and auth were healthy.

findings.claim: Outbox backlog built up mid-window: publications fell to ~19/10s against 32/10s arrivals, and pending reached 123 with oldest age 38s.
findings.reason: Per-bucket counts and pending/age samples show delivery fell behind and then drained to 3.

findings.claim: The transfers API was healthy, so lateness is downstream of the request path.
findings.reason: All 476 requests returned 201, p99 0.25s, and no errors.

findings.claim: Delivery slowness is from consumer handler time (p95 405ms vs p50 0.025ms), not auth or network errors.
findings.reason: All 477 attempts succeeded with zero failures; auth p95 is 78ms; handler p95 is 405ms, which would cap serial delivery throughput.

limitations: Only the first 30 delivery logs are listed, so slow attempts are not tied to the backlog time range.
The consumer is a test fixture, and the handler slowness could be an artifact of the fixture rather than a real consumer.
next_checks: Correlate slow handler attempts (~405ms) with the 09:54-09:56 backlog window, and check the poller's concurrency and batch size.
Check consumer-side logs for what caused the 405ms handler time and why it recovered at the end.

alternatives.reason: Failed gauge stayed 0, and all 477 attempts succeeded on attempt 1.
alternatives.hypothesis: Delivery failures or retries caused the delay

alternatives.reason: Consumer auth p95 is 77.7ms, which is stable and small relative to the 405ms handler time.

report.summary: Notifications were delayed by an outbox publication backlog. Publication throughput fell to about 60% of arrivals, then drained. The consumer handler's slow phase is the likely limiter, but the evidence does not prove it.

findings.claim: The transfer API was healthy, while the outbox publication rate lagged arrivals for roughly 100 s, building a backlog.
findings.reason: The API returned 476 201s with no errors. Arrivals ran at 32 per 10 s while publications ran at 15-20 per 10 s, and pending reached 123.

findings.claim: Notification delay grew with the backlog: oldest undelivered age rose from 0.66 s to 38 s, then recovered once publications caught up (77-81 per 10 s).
findings.reason: The age samples climb with pending and drop back to 0.66 s at 09:56:23 after the catch-up buckets.

findings.claim: Deliveries all succeeded, with no failures or retries. Slow attempts (~480 ms vs ~72 ms) were dominated by consumer handler time (p95 405 ms), not auth or network.
findings.reason: 477 of 477 attempts succeeded on attempt 1. Consumer handler p95 is 405 ms against a p50 of 0.025 ms, and auth stays near 70 ms.

findings.claim: The consumer's slow handler phase probably reduced serial publication throughput to ~19 per 10 s, which would explain the backlog.
findings.reason: About 19 publications per 10 s is roughly 0.5 s each, which matches the ~480 ms slow attempts. No tool shows the publisher is serial.

alternatives.hypothesis: The publisher itself stalled or was throttled, independent of consumer latency.
alternatives.reason: No publisher-side metrics are available. The catch-up burst is consistent with a publisher pause, though it also fits the consumer recovering.

alternatives.hypothesis: Network or auth errors caused the delay.
alternatives.reason: There were zero auth, network and server errors. Auth latency was stable at about 70 ms.

limitations: Only the earliest 100 of 477 delivery records are listed, so the slow period is only partly visible per record.
There is no consumer-side explanation for why the handler was slow, and the pending gauge is sampled at scrape times.
next_checks: Correlate per-attempt handler time with publication timestamps across the full window to confirm serial dispatch is the limiter.
Inspect the consumer handler and the publisher's concurrency settings for the slow phase starting about 09:54:00.
